1. Open the diamonds dataset from ggplot2. 
```{r}
data(diamonds)
```

2. Run a correlation between the x and y variables. What do you notice? 
```{r}
cor(diamonds$x, diamonds$y)
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
cor.test(diamonds$x, diamonds$y)

#they have a very strong correlation at 0.97! I made a graph just to visualize it for myself and notice there are a few outliers here but otherwise the correlation seems super linear.
```

3. What is the correlation between price and carat?
```{r}
cor(diamonds$price, diamonds$carat)
cor.test(diamonds$price, diamonds$carat)

#correlation is 0.92
```

4. Create a linear model predicting price from table. What is the coefficient for table? 
```{r}
priceLM<- lm(price~ table, data = diamonds)
summary(priceLM)

#coefficients are -9109.05 and 226.98
```

5. Run a regression and an Anova predicting price from color. What do you notice about the two types of output? 
```{r}
otherPriceLM<- lm(price ~ color, data = diamonds)
summary(otherPriceLM)

priceAnov<- aov(price ~ color, data = diamonds)
summary(priceAnov)

#I get a lot more information from the linear regression, including information on all of the separate colors. Both seem helpful but I'd probably steer towards a linear regression for getting more numbers off the bat.
```

6. Run a t test to determine if "D" color diamonds are more expensive than "E" color diamonds.
```{r}
DEDiamonds<- subset(diamonds, color == c("D", "E"))
#making a new dataset with just D and E diamonds is the only way I could think of to make this work

t.test(price ~ color, data = DEDiamonds, alternative = "greater")
#diamonds in D are more expensive than E on average
```

7. Open the warpbreaks dataset. What test would you use to determine the correlation between wool type and breaks?
```{r}
data(warpbreaks)
```

8. What is the correlation between wool type and breaks? 
```{r}
warpbreaks$numWool<- as.numeric(warpbreaks$wool)
cor(warpbreaks$numWool, warpbreaks$breaks)

#it has a pretty weak negative correlation at -0.22
```

9. A student has a 35 question, multiple choice test. Each question has 4 choices. If they answered 17 questions correctly, did their responses differ from chance?
```{r}
binom.test(17, 35, p = 0.25)
#Yes, their response was not by chance, because their p- value of 0.003 is less than a standard alpha value of 0.05
```
